questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to live in a European city - preferably France.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Hard, Erasmus coordinator and TSE coordinator were not the most helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: At the end of the first week, there was a welcome "coffee" for Erasmus students in French, but there I got the opportunity to meet other Erasmus students, who could then help with questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Small studio rooms with own bathroom and fridge. Some had a small kitchenette in their room, but you don't get to choose when you apply through KU, you just get assigned to one.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There are sharing kitchens and the school has a Restaurant/cafeteria, which is open for lunch and dinner. Price is around 3 euros.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Rooms are very small but very close to everything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Very confusing, some of the classes that I had planned on taking overlapped so I had to take some other classes. The school moved around the schedule even when classes had started.
Also most registration was in French.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an Erasmus coordinator and a TSE international relations officer. But they were not that much help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the classes I wanted, only had to change 2 out of 7.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There will be some changes in the online learning agreement, and it can be very chaotic in the beginning.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Generally I think the level of the courses are lower than Economics at KU. But the ECTS for each course are very small (3-5 ECTS) so you have around 7-8 courses, which can be a bit chaotic.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Slower pace. Minimal use of computer in class. Also, note that all exams are by hand (some you get to use an old school calculator).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced Micro, Public Economics, Development Economics, Environmental and Ressource economics, Economic du Climat, Market Finance, Behavioral and Experimental Economics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Environmental and Ressource economics & Behavioral and Experimental Economics were a good mix of lectures, group work and individual work.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was not unexpected but it is a good idea to count travelling to other cities in the budget.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
McSmart Meal Deal 5 euro.
Cigarettes, 13 euros.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
School offers lots of sports, but they get filled up very quickly.
Also school offers French courses, which were great.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Find ESN and BDETSE on instagram and join what's app groups to find out what social activities there are. AEGEE toulouse was great, Francois the owner plans many great (more intimate) events for Erasmus students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Bordeaux, Montpellier or a hike in the Pyrénées. Also there are a lot of nice small cities around Toulouse, which you can visit for day-trips. If you want to go to the sea Collioure and Marseille are also very nice. 1 euro train in all Occitanie the first weekend of each month, book in advance.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy I didn't really think about it.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to speak french.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Most of the French are not very good at speaking English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The French cuisine.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go to as many events in the beginning and meet people.
Go out and drink some wine.
Use the pool at Chapou in summer time, city gets very hot, only 1.5 euro.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Buy your own soap for washing machines

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Made friends for life

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not being very good at speaking French

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
